newsitem.title: INDIA: Indonesia says decision on ASEAN entries by July.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says decision on ASEAN entries by July.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Tuesday the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) planned to decide by July whether to admit Burma, Laos and Cambodia to the forum.

"We will have a meeting of foreign ministers of ASEAN some time before July in order to decide what to recommend to our heads of government," Alatas, in India for a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), told Reuters.
ASEAN leaders agreed at an informal summit in Jakarta late last year that Burma, Laos and Cambodia would be admitted simultaneously, but no date was set.
Alatas said the ASEAN ministers had touched on the topic in discussions on Monday but had made no decision.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn told Reuters the ministers planned to meet in Kuala Lumpur next month to discuss the matter.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
The seven ASEAN members, as well as Burma, Laos and Cambodia, are also in the 113-member Non-Aligned Movement.
